# Services the gateway smoke test exercises, one service_name per line.
#
# Each line runs ONLY that service's "Connectivity test" document (not its
# code examples or anything else) via `usvc seller services run-tests
# --document-id <connectivity-doc-id> --include-active --force`. Keep this
# list short: each entry is chosen because it is the cheapest way to prove a
# DISTINCT gateway code path or cross-system integration actually works, not
# because the service itself is important.
#
# ── API gateway: LLM passthrough, basic connectivity (relocated from
#    apisix-gateways#23 — see unitysvc/.github#<TBD> for the move) ──
#
# Trimmed to just openai (2026-09-06): the original 5-service set each
# proved a DISTINCT gateway code path (openai/anthropic translation +
# streaming, nebius's gzip'd SSE, cohere's upstream_path override, bedrock's
# SigV4 signing) — deliberately dropped in favor of one simple, reliable
# check, since nebius/Qwen/Qwen3-32B kept failing on an upstream-account
# issue unrelated to the gateway (genuine upstream_fault, not our bug) and
# that noise wasn't worth carrying for a post-deploy smoke test. If deeper
# per-code-path coverage is wanted again later, apisix-gateways#23's history
# has the full rationale for each of the four dropped services.

# Plain OpenAI -> OpenAI passthrough with an UNCOMPRESSED event stream. The
# control: if this breaks, something very general broke.
openai/gpt-4.1-nano

# ── API gateway: HTTP relay + cross-system integration (Redis, Celery) ──
# Motivated by the msg-to-mailbox incident (2026-09): a production redeploy
# left routing silently broken and nothing caught it until a human happened
# to test the one broken service by hand.

# API gateway -> HTTP relay -> platform sink, verifiable by polling the sink's
# own /retrieve API for the forwarded request (not just a 2xx from the
# gateway). Private, smoke-test-only service (unitysvc-services-http).
http-to-sink

# ── SMTP gateway: outbound SMTP relay and HTTP bridge ──
# Confirms the Haraka SMTP gateway is up, authenticates, and can dispatch —
# also exercises Redis (route/customer-context lookups) and Celery (every
# run-tests diagnostic dispatches via run_service_diagnostic).

# SMTP gateway -> SMTP relay -> platform mailpit sink.
smtp-relay

# SMTP gateway -> HTTP bridge -> platform sink, verifiable via sink's
# /retrieve API (smtp-to-msg's code example already does this; the
# connectivity test itself only proves the SMTP greeting).
smtp-to-http

# SMTP gateway -> API gateway (http-to-sink) -> platform sink, verifiable
# via sink's /retrieve API. The one path that proves the SMTP and API
# gateways can reach each other cross-container, not just each work in
# isolation. What looked like a hairpin-NAT/loopback flake
# (2026-09-06 investigation notes) was actually ${API_GATEWAY_BASE_URL}
# never being substituted in upstream_access_config.base_url — fixed by
# smtp-gateway#9's render_gateway_macros, using auth_mode: forward instead
# of api_key: __forward__ (unitysvc-services-smtp#33) so base_url can stay
# the portable macro instead of a hardcoded literal.
smtp-to-apisix-gateway

# ── S3 gateway ──

# S3 gateway proxy of platform-owned content.
s3-proxy
